brief.todays_call: The earned-dollar side is losing altitude as the oil claim widens. July remittance held $2.86bn — a second straight month under $3bn — while Brent at $94.09 sits well up from its $71.18 window low, lifting the import bill inflows must cover. Reserves last printed $36.42bn on the 31 Jul print, cover 5.96mo on the May read; exports $4.2bn on the Jun read, the taka firm at 122.07. Both inflow engines are flat as the oil bill rises. The book stays defensive on the peg — long reserve visibility, reading a firm taka as demand weakness, not dollar strength.

sections.verdict: Book frozen — NPLs 32.26% on Q1, capital cushion gone.
sections.analysis: The banking book is unchanged and the freeze is still the story: NPLs 32.26% on the Q1 2026 print, system CAR 1.56% on Q3 2025 — 844bp below the 10% floor, a cushion gone rather than thin. Neither number moves until Q2 disclosure lands the court-stayed loan stock that already understates the headline. What moves is the scaffolding: BB has floated loan-recovery mediation and an alternative dispute-resolution track, and the sell-side is running 'how the sector stabilised' copy. All of it repairs the tail; none of it restarts the engine. Private credit sits at 4.98% — liquidity is not the constraint, creditworthy demand is. Dispersion stays the trade: own the private compounders, fade the SCB paper the resolution regime tests first.

sections.verdict: Brent at $94.09, up from its $71.18 window low.
sections.analysis: Crude is the day's cleanest one-way read into the book, with the widest reach. Brent holds $94.09 and WTI $86.85 — the barrel has climbed off a $71.18 window low and now sits near the top of its three-month range. The transmission into Bangladesh is direct and compounding: each dollar re-widens an import bill the earned-dollar side already strains to cover, with July remittance at $2.86bn and exports $4.2bn on the Jun read. It also threatens the inflation turn the MPC awaits — non-food CPI prints 9.61% on the Jun read, energy cost-push not yet in the base. Crude is now the swing variable across FX, fiscal and macro at once — position for a wider import bill and a later, shallower easing path if Brent holds above $90 into the next prints.

sections.verdict: Remittance held $2.86bn — a second month under $3bn as oil bites.
sections.analysis: Remittance is the earned-dollar engine that has to cover the gap the trade account cannot, and it is losing altitude. July printed $2.86bn — a second straight month under $3bn — and it is well off the $3.76bn high the series reached over the past year. The other side of the runway is widening: Brent holds $94.09, up from a $71.18 window low, lifting the import bill soft demand had masked. And the buffer behind both is stale — reserves last printed $36.42bn on the 31 Jul print, cover 5.96mo on the May read, the August refresh overdue. Neither engine is broken; exports hold $4.2bn on the Jun read, the taka is firm at 122.07. But the trajectory has turned: inflows flat, the oil bill rising, the reserve check unpaid. The book stays defensive on the peg — long reserve visibility, reading a firm taka as demand weakness, not dollar strength.

chart_read.implication: Treasury: earned-dollar cover thinning as the oil bill rises — watch whether $2.86bn is a floor or a slide.

banker_read.verdict: July remittance held $2.86bn — a second straight month under $3bn — while the buffer stopped rebuilding: reserves $36.42bn on the 31 Jul print, cover 5.96mo on the May read. Both earned-dollar engines are soft, exports $4.2bn on the Jun read, and Brent at $94.09 now pulls the other way.
